Forgot your password? Forgot your username? Lost the phone that gives you
sign-in codes? This page gets you back in. It takes about two minutes, and
you do not need to know anything about computers beyond copy and paste.

## Why there is no "email me a link"

Biryar runs on your own computer, not on ours. We do not hold your account,
your password or your email address, so we cannot send you a reset link, and
neither can anyone else. What proves the account is yours is simpler: you
are sitting at the computer Biryar runs on.

If someone else looks after Biryar for your business, ask them to follow
this page for you. It works for any account on that computer.

## What to do

**1. Go to the computer Biryar runs on.** That is the one where it was
installed, which may not be the one you usually open it from.

**2. Make sure Docker is running.** On Windows and Mac, open Docker Desktop
and wait until it says it is running. On Linux it already is.

**3. Open a terminal.** This is a window you type commands into.

- **Windows:** press the Windows key, type `PowerShell`, press Enter.
- **Mac:** press Command and Space together, type `Terminal`, press Enter.
- **Linux:** press Ctrl, Alt and T together.

It does not matter which folder the terminal opens in.

**4. Copy this line, paste it into the terminal, and press Enter.**

```
docker exec -it biryar-api-1 biryar-password
```

Paste it exactly as it is. There is nothing in it to change.

**5. Answer its questions.** It asks at most three, described below. Nothing
is changed until you have answered all of them, so you can close the window
at any point and your account stays as it was.

**6. Open Biryar and sign in.** The last line it prints tells you which name
to sign in with.

## The questions it asks

Here is what a whole run looks like. What you type is marked.

```
Getting back into Biryar. Nothing is changed until every question is answered.

The accounts on this machine:

  1. anna    anna@example.com    owner
  2. david   david@example.com   assistant

Which one is yours? Type its number, its username or its email: 1        <- you

What do you need?

  1. A new password
  2. A new phone: mine is lost or replaced, so set up the sign-in code again
  3. Both

Type 1, 2 or 3, then Enter (Enter alone means 1): 1                      <- you

Choose a new password, type it and press Enter. Nothing shows while you type.
It needs at least 12 characters, with at least one that is not a letter or a digit
and at least one capital letter or digit.
Or press Enter on its own, and one is made for you.

New password:                                                            <- you
The same again:                                                          <- you

Password set for anna@example.com (Anna, owner).

Now open Biryar and sign in as anna with your new password.
```

**Which account is yours.** You do not have to remember your username. The
accounts on the computer are shown first, each with its username and its
email. Type the number in front of yours, or its username, or its email:
all three work. If there is only one account, it shows that one and you
just press Enter.

**What you need.** This is only asked if your account uses sign-in codes
from a phone. Choose 1 for a forgotten password, 2 for a lost or replaced
phone, 3 for both.

**Your new password.** You have two choices:

- **Choose your own.** Type it and press Enter, then type it once more.
  Nothing appears on the screen while you type, not even dots. That is
  normal: it keeps the password from being read over your shoulder. It
  needs at least 12 characters, with at least one that is not a letter or a
  digit (a comma or a dash, for example) and at least one capital letter or
  digit. If it is too weak, or the two did not match, you are simply asked
  again.
- **Have one made for you.** Press Enter without typing anything. A strong
  password is shown on the screen, once. Write it down or put it in your
  password manager before you close the window, because it cannot be shown
  again.

## If you forgot your username

Step 5 shows it to you. You also do not need it to sign in: the sign-in box
takes your username or your email address, whichever you remember.

## If you lost or replaced your phone

Follow the steps above and choose 2, or 3 if you want a new password as
well. Biryar forgets the old phone and signs you out everywhere. The next
time you sign in, it shows a new code to scan with the authenticator app on
your new phone, exactly as it did the first time.

## If the line does not work

| The terminal says | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `No such container: biryar-api-1` | Biryar is not running, or runs under another name. | Type `docker ps` and press Enter. If a name ending in `api-1` is listed, use that name in place of `biryar-api-1`. If nothing is listed, Biryar is not running: see [after the machine restarts](/setup/install/#after-the-machine-restarts). |
| `Cannot connect to the Docker daemon` or `error during connect` | Docker is not running. | Open Docker Desktop, wait until it says it is running, and try again. |
| `the input device is not a TTY` | This kind of terminal cannot answer questions. | On Windows use PowerShell, not Git Bash. |
| `biryar-password: not found` | This copy of Biryar is older than the command. | [Update Biryar](/setup/install/#updating), then try again. Or use the longer line below. |

The longer line, for an older copy. Here you do have to change something:
replace `<your username or email>`, including the two angle brackets, with
your own. It makes a new password for you and shows it once.

```
docker exec -it biryar-api-1 python -m biryar.passwd --login <your username or email>
```

For example, for the username `anna`:

```
docker exec -it biryar-api-1 python -m biryar.passwd --login anna
```

## Without a terminal, on Windows and Mac

Docker Desktop can do the same from its own window.

1. Open Docker Desktop and click **Containers** on the left.
2. Click **biryar** to open it, then click the line that ends in **api-1**.
3. Click the **Exec** tab. A small terminal opens inside it.
4. Type `biryar-password`, press Enter, and answer the questions as above.

## Is this safe?

Yes, and it adds no new way in. Anyone who can sit at the computer and run
this line could already read everything Biryar stores there. So the thing
to protect is the computer itself: give it a password of its own, and do
not leave it unlocked where others can reach it.

## For people who script it

The same command takes its answers as options, and then asks nothing:

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--login NAME` | Whose account, by username or email. |
| `--ask` | Ask for the password instead of making one. |
| `--reset-two-factor` | Forget the phone. The password is left alone unless `--ask` or `--new-password` is also given. |
| `--new-password` | With `--reset-two-factor`, also make a new password. |
| `--tenant SLUG` | Which business, on an installation that holds more than one. |
